questions.q: What is human capital formation, and what are its main sources?

answer.text: Human capital is the stock of skill, knowledge, good health and abilities present in the people of a country, which makes them more productive. Human capital formation is the process of building up this stock, that is, of turning human beings into a more productive and valuable resource through investment in them.

There are several sources. Education is the most important, as it imparts knowledge and skills. Investment in health keeps people fit and able to work. On-the-job training improves the skills of workers already employed. Migration, from villages to cities or abroad, can raise earnings and productivity. Finally, spending on information about the job market and education helps people use their skills well.

answer: By investing in these sources, a country raises the productivity and well-being of its people, which in turn drives economic growth.

questions.q: How does human capital formation contribute to economic growth?

answer.text: is the building up of skill, knowledge and health in people, and it is a key driver of economic growth.
